material.text_fr: Dans le tiroir d'Odile, un Polaroid : un port, des bateaux, et « 1971 » au dos.
Vous avez promis à M. Marchand de retrouver le peintre « L. » avant son anniversaire.
Aider Margaux à refaire la carte du Mistral avant le printemps.
L'avenir du Mistral : le garder, le changer, ou le laisser partir ?
Gus a reçu une lettre d'un notaire, avec un timbre étranger, et il ne l'ouvre pas.
Romy vous a demandé d'être la voix française de son documentaire radio.
Lila et Berlin : peut-on vouloir quelqu'un ici, et vouloir son départ pour elle ?
Qui était Odile, et pourquoi est-elle partie ?
Rue de Lancry, au troisième, une fenêtre est encore allumée.

departed.name: Lila Bonnet
departed.why: Lila left for Berlin on 8 January (T8, the platform) and lives there now.

rules: The whole cast knows the learner: never a stranger's welcome, never the vous of strangers from the group.
The continuation may look for «L.», ask about the rue de Lancry, follow the painting; it never reveals who L. is — that answer belongs to the next authored season.
facts: The learner kept Odile's flat above Le Mistral and lives there now.
Le Mistral is exactly as it was; Margaux runs it alone, on a nine-year lease.
M. Marchand left the building for a residence without stairs; Solvel owns his floors, he kept the café's walls.
Only four people know Odile's notebook page; Gus knows nothing of it.
The painting «Le Mistral sur le canal» is with the learner; its back reads «Pour Odile, qui part. — L., 1970» and «Toujours rue de Lancry. — L., 2021».
Marin has put his co-op folder in a drawer.
Lila left for Berlin on 8 January; she lives there now. She writes; she is never in a Paris scene.
Odile's last letter has been read: she left two things in Paris, the flat and someone; for the other, «regarde derrière le tableau du Mistral».
Camille Marchand has met the learner and still says vous; the switch to tu belongs to a later season.
The café question of season 1 is closed. Do not reopen it.
M. Marchand comes to Sunday lunch at the learner's, by the 46 bus, as he did at Odile's.
Romy gave the learner the memory card with Margaux's admission, without a word.

draft.logline: A Polaroid in Odile's drawer points to a Breton port and a year—1971. You go there with Romy and Marin to follow a photographer's trail, keep a promise to M. Marchand about the painter 'L.', and help Gus face a foreign letter; the shore remembers things Paris has forgotten, and the season listens for a ghost that may be memory, not spectre.
draft.logline_fr: Un Polaroid mène au port d'Odile. Vous partez en Bretagne pour chercher des indices et tenir une promesse.
draft.your_arc: You follow the Polaroid: the trip is both a search for the painter L. and a quiet reckoning with Odile's past; by the end you keep the mystery intact but bring back a living thread that ties the learner to Odile more strongly.
draft.first_episode_seed: Romy arrives with the Polaroid; she says, simply, «Il faut aller voir.» You tell Margaux you will leave for a week — Marin and Gus come with you — and you find a ferry timetable in Odile's drawer with 'Douarnenez 1971' penciled on the back of a receipt.

stages.summary: Romy shows you the Polaroid and insists you go to the port in the photo; you book the ferry and Marin offers his family contacts.
At the Douarnenez harbour you discover a boat name and a ledgers entry dated 1971 that matches marks on the Polaroid; the clue is small and ambiguous.
You trace a ledger entry to a pension owner (Madeleine) who keeps a memory of a painter who stayed in 1971 but refuses to reveal a full name — a crucial lead remains incomplete but alive.
You remember your promise to M. Marchand to find 'L.' before his birthday and decide to ask local elders in Douarnenez for any painter who painted the port.
Jean-Luc and other locals recall a quiet artist who slept in the pension and painted at dusk; their stories conflict about a surname and a studio address.

You locate a small label on an old canvas in Madeleine's attic that reads only an initial and a year; you deliver the discovery to M. Marchand but it does not reveal 'L.' — the promise is honored as search, not as answer.
Gus brings the foreign-stamped letter and asks you to help him find where it was mailed; the stamp suggests a port city route and the envelope smells faintly of seaweed.
The postal mark is partial; Yann remembers a 1970s shipping company that forwarded correspondence via Douarnenez and points you toward a former office now a workshop.

Gus chooses whether to open the letter in public; he does, and the contents are a short, affectionate postcard dated 1971 addressed to 'Pour O.' — it confirms a connection to Odile's era but not the painter's name.
Romy wants to record local voices for her radio documentary and asks you to be the French voice — she is torn between a story that reaches a wider audience and the risk of hurting friends.
Your interviews with Madeleine and Jean-Luc surface an anecdote about Odile that could change how people see her; Romy hears a confession on tape that might embarrass Margaux and the group.

Romy decides how to shape the piece: she leaves the most damaging clip out and includes a quieter sequence that honours Odile's complexity; trust among friends is maintained but the documentary gains depth.

open_threads.text: Who was Odile, and why did she leave? The season finds more memory, but the full answer remains for later.
open_threads.text_fr: Qui était Odile, et pourquoi est-elle partie ?

open_threads.text: Can you want someone's freedom and still love them? Lila's departure to Berlin touches the learner's question about letting people go.
open_threads.text_fr: Peut-on vouloir partir pour quelqu'un et rester aimé ?

open_threads.text: Rue de Lancry, the third-floor light is still on in memory — there is a line in Odile's notes that points back to that window; the season listens but does not enter that room.
open_threads.text_fr: Rue de Lancry, au troisième, une fenêtre reste allumée dans les souvenirs.

setting.neighborhood: le vieux port et l'étier — conserverie, quais de granit, maisons basses
setting.genre: maritime mystery with gentle ghost-story echoes
setting.tone: misty, careful, quietly uncanny — a mystery that feels like memory
setting.situation: You travel to Douarnenez with Romy and Marin to follow a Polaroid and keep a promise about the painter L.; the town asks for patience rather than answers.
setting.situation_fr: Vous allez à Douarnenez avec Romy et Marin pour suivre le Polaroid et tenir votre promesse.
setting.why: The Polaroid of a port (p:polaroid_port), found in Odile's drawer and given weight by Romy's investigation, pulls you to a real harbour—Douarnenez—where family ties (Marin's Finistère roots) and Gus's foreign-stamped letter (p:lettre_gus) converge;

places.description: The granite quay of a working fishing port where old fishermen mend nets and a faded photo might have been taken; key scenes of arrival, searching registries, and a late-night visit when the tide and memory return.
places.brief: Granite quay, coiled ropes and iron bollards, a rusted lamp-post; low late-afternoon light with sea-spray, gulls in silhouette.

places.name_fr: Le Café-Pension de la rue du Port
places.description: A low-ceilinged café that is also a small pension; locals gossip over tea and the owner keeps letters under the register — a place for interviews and the kind of memory that won't leave a shelf.
places.brief: Wooden counter with brass bell, a shelf of tin can labels and old postcards, a bay window looking to the quay; warm candle-like interior light against grey morning outside.

places.description: A small lighthouse at the mouth of the estuary where one can look back toward town and imagine the port of 1971; an alone place for late revelations and a quiet, ghostly moment with wind and light.
places.brief: Whitewashed tower on black rock, a single red lantern, a low tide of exposed mussel beds; cold, horizontal dawn light and long shadows.

places.description: A low municipal archive room with dusty ledgers of boats, addresses, and registrations — where a 1971 shipping list or artist address might be found and questions are answered slowly.
places.brief: Filing cabinets and a long wooden table, a fan of old maps pinned to the wall, a green-shaded desk lamp; thin morning light from a small window, dust motes visible.

places.description: A small stone house at the back of the port belonging to a retired fisherman who remembers faces and names from decades ago — a place of memory and a living link to Marin's family.
places.brief: Low stone façade with a blue door, drying lobsterman's ropes on a peg, a windowsill of herbs; late afternoon amber light, smell of sea and smoked wood.

new_characters.name: Yann Le Goff
new_characters.role: Harbour master and unofficial archivist of the port; knows small, local histories and who left where in 1971.
new_characters.personality: Quietly authoritative, precise with dates, slow to trust outsiders but proud of his port.
new_characters.wants: To keep the town's stories honest and to be the one who remembers names correctly.
new_characters.speech_pattern: Measured, uses local Breton expressions sparingly, speaks kindly but with pauses.

new_characters.name: Madeleine Bréhat
new_characters.role: Owner of the café-pension; keeps letters under the counter and remembers guests from decades past, including someone who painted the port.
new_characters.personality: Warm, sharp-eyed, with a habit of humming old sea shanties; protective of her town's reputation.
new_characters.wants: To protect the delicate peace of the port and to ensure newcomers do not break what is held here.
new_characters.speech_pattern: Fast, affectionate, adds small anecdotes to every sentence.

new_characters.name: Jean-Luc Cadoret
new_characters.role: Retired fisherman and old friend of Marin's father; remembers faces and can place a photo to a year or a boat name.
new_characters.personality: Grumpy but kind, fond of small ceremonies like mending nets and telling exact dates.
new_characters.wants: To be useful to Marin and to keep family memories intact.
new_characters.speech_pattern: Short sentences, a scratching laugh, often begins with 'Tu sais...'.

interlude.reason_fr: Entre deux saisons : l'histoire reprend le 3 janvier.
